what_changed: CFPB interpretive rule stating that the FCRA generally preempts state laws touching broad areas of credit reporting; replaces the July 2022 interpretive rule withdrawn in May 2025. Applicable October 28, 2025.
compliant_agent_must_now: Furnishers: the CFPB's view is that state credit-reporting laws in areas the FCRA regulates are generally preempted. This is interpretive; state laws are not repealed and courts may differ, so do not stop complying with a state furnishing rule on this basis without counsel.
open_questions_for_deploying_team: Which state credit-reporting or furnishing laws (e.g., medical debt or coerced debt reporting bans) does the deployment currently follow, and should any be reassessed under this interpretation?
rationale: Interpretive rule on preemption of state credit-reporting laws; affects which state furnishing rules apply to furnishers. The register has no state credit-reporting rows, so this may be a register gap. Stage A: title, abstract, metadata and eCFR diff excerpt only; full text not read.
